Definition: from G5384 and G3056; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian:--Philologus.
BiblicalUsage: Philologos is a Christian at Rome whom Paul greets, and his name means fond of words, talkative. Paul sends his greeting to Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Philologus is one more name in the long greeting that proves the church is personal: Paul names them one by one, and God knows them all.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
